title: gdpr.erasure.request
description: Open an erasure for one subject and get its identity back. The synchronous half of gdpr.erasure.open, for a caller that must record the request id (to link its own row to the erasure, or to show "pending deletion until X" straight away). Same payload, same request, same idempotency: a repeat of the same idempotency_key returns the EXISTING request — {request_id, due_at, state} of the row that is already open — instead of a second one. Response: {"request_id": integer, "due_at": string (ISO-8601), "state": "queued"|"erasing"|"deleted"|"timeout"}. Raises on a subject_type outside STAPEL_GDPR["SUBJECT_TYPES"]. A comm call carries no session: as with every Function, this is as authoritative as the transport that reaches it, so a host exposing it over HTTP puts it behind its own service credential.

subject_key.description: The host's own id for that subject (a user id for "account").

workspace_id.description: Workspace the subject belongs to, for owners that partition their stores by it.

requested_by.description: User id of whoever asked, when a person did.

origin.description: Why this erasure exists. Defaults to "user".

idempotency_key.description: De-duplication key, unique across erasures. Same key = same request.
